key_insight: Fine image detail does not always need image-wide communication. SpecSlot separates global structure modeling from local detail modeling, aiming to increase output detail without proportionally increasing costly global attention.
problem_solved: Pixel-space generative Transformers typically assign one token to each image patch. Capturing finer detail therefore requires more tokens, making global attention increasingly expensive.
method: Introduce SpecSlot, a pixel-space rectified-flow Transformer.
Use global information exchange for low-frequency structure, such as overall shapes and layout.
Model high-frequency detail locally to reduce its dependence on global token communication.
impact: This approach could make detailed pixel-space generation more computationally efficient by reserving global attention for information that needs it. The provided abstract is truncated, so specific architectural details and performance gains cannot be confirmed.
visual_elements: Split image showing low-frequency shapes and layout versus high-frequency edges and textures.
Side-by-side diagrams contrasting globally connected patch tokens with global structure exchange plus local detail modeling.
Conceptual flow diagram: global structure modeling + local detail modeling → generated image.
Token-grid illustration showing why finer patches increase global attention cost.
paper_title: Read, Allocate, Route: Role-Coupled Tokenization for Pixel-Space Generative Transformers
paper_authors: Jiongfan Yang, Weichen Fan, Haiwen Diao, Zhongang Cai, Ziwei Liu
